editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, clear prose; appropriately covers the regulatory mechanics (FMVSS No. 135 changes, telltale relocation, stopping-distance redefinition, AV STEP withdrawal) alongside the competitive angle (Tesla Cybercab, Zoox, Waymo) and critical context (safety-incident backdrop, NHTSA staffing cuts). Word count (810) is within the News category range (400-1200).
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots were read in full from sources/2026-07/nhtsa-proposes-dropping-manual-brake-pedal-mandate-for-driverless-vehicles-clearing-a-path-for-teslas-cybercab/ (source-0.html.gz TechCrunch, source-1.html.gz The Register, source-2.html.gz Crowell & Moring, source-3.html.gz The Drive). All 4 fetched live at HTTP 200 (no archive_fallback). Decompressed sha256 of every file was independently recomputed and matched the manifest exactly, confirming snapshot integrity. Every direct quote in the article (Morrison's 'cusp of the greatest technological revolution...' quote, the Crowell 'clearly visible to occupants...' and 'from the point at which the electronic braking command is transmitted' quotes, the Register 'manually operated driving control...misuse by a vehicle passenger' and 'gutted during Tesla CEO Elon Musk's time...' and 'is still maturing...' quotes, The Drive's 'testing Cybercabs without human inputs in Austin' and 'taking no position at this time...' quotes) was verified verbatim against its respective snapshot and correctly attributed. TechCrunch's Zoox/Waymo paragraph and the Biden-era steering-wheel rule sentence are near-verbatim paraphrases of TechCrunch text, correctly attributed. One finding: the sentence 'a separate recall of "over 3,800 robotaxis" by Waymo "over risk entering closed construction zones," according to [The Drive]' is NOT supported by The Drive's snapshot — the words '3,800', 'construction', and 'recall' do not appear anywhere in that source (confirmed by exhaustive grep of the extracted text of all 4 snapshots; the figure appears nowhere in any of the 4 cited sources). Independent web research confirms the underlying fact is real and accurate (Waymo recalled ~3,800-3,900 robotaxis in June 2026 over freeway construction-zone incidents, reported by CNBC, Gizmodo, Detroit News, Washington Times, Planetizen) but none of those outlets are cited in this submission — the article fabricated a citation (including fabricated quotation marks) to The Drive for a true fact that outlet never reported. This is a misattributed/fabricated-citation issue on an otherwise-accurate subordinate detail, not a fabricated event.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Central thesis (NHTSA NPRM proposing to drop the manual brake pedal mandate for driverless-only vehicles, benefiting Tesla's Cybercab) is fully and independently corroborated across all 4 sources plus outside verification (NHTSA's own press release, CNBC, Insurance Journal, Lexology, Mondaq all confirm the same proposal). The Overview's date claim ('proposed on June 25, 2026,' cited to TechCrunch) was cross-checked: TechCrunch and CNBC both published same-day coverage on June 25, 2026, while Crowell & Moring's client alert and The Register (published Friday, June 26) date NHTSA's formal action to June 26, 2026. This is a genuine one-day ambiguity present in the real-world reporting itself (agencies often issue a press release a day ahead of, or same-day as, the Federal Register/docket posting picked up by legal alerts) rather than an invented date; the article's phrasing ('proposed on June 25, 2026 ... according to TechCrunch') accurately reflects what its cited source reported and is not treated as an error requiring correction. The one confirmed factual/citation problem is the misattributed Waymo recall statistic addressed above.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The automated 'loaded language' finding (pattern match on 'clearly') was manually reviewed and is a false positive: the flagged word occurs solely inside a verbatim quotation from Crowell & Moring's client alert ('clearly visible to occupants in all designated seating positions'), correctly rendered in quote marks and attributed — not editorial language inserted by the bot. No correction needed for this finding.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers this NHTSA brake-pedal NPRM (checked src/content/articles/2026-06/ and src/content/articles/2026-07/ for 'NHTSA' and 'brake pedal' — no hits). The article's internal link to /article/2026-04/03-tesla-begins-cybercab-mass-production-at-giga-texas-as-safety-record-and-regulatory-path-remain-uncertain was verified to point to an existing published article. This is a genuinely new story, not a duplicate.
concerns: The sentence attributing an 'over 3,800 robotaxis' / 'over risk entering closed construction zones' Waymo recall to The Drive is not supported by The Drive's cited article; the fact is true and independently verifiable (CNBC, Gizmodo, Detroit News, Washington Times all reported ~3,800-3,900 robotaxis recalled over freeway construction-zone incidents in June 2026) but was reported by outlets this submission did not cite. Filing a corrections record.
recommendations: Future submissions should cite the actual outlet a specific statistic came from rather than attaching an existing citation from elsewhere in the article to an uncited fact.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News article on a real and significant regulatory development. Three of four sources check out cleanly across every quote and specific claim; the fourth (The Drive) is correctly used for two verified quotes but is also, incorrectly, the attribution for one unrelated true-but-uncited statistic. This is a single recoverable misattribution in a subordinate paragraph (What We Don't Know), not in the headline, summary, or lead — appropriate for APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS with a public corrections record.
